messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: policy-engine runtime panic in 'smart-region-fallback' during routing. Multiple requests returned 5xx and we observed repeated cross-region fallbacks. Error: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference at eval.go:234. Affected service: routing-policy-evaluator. Spike started ~1993001098, currently elevated error rate ~7% for text-generation routes. Auto-fallback selected smaller model_variant 'gpt-small-quant' for some traffic, causing correctness regressions and customer complaints. See trace ids: trace=tr-9a8f, tr-9a90.
carla (oncall): Acknowledged. Paging oncall rotation and triage. I'm oncall now, will take lead. @samir can you grab logs and stack trace? @ops-bot open incident ticket.
ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-334. Severity: P2. Pagerduty alerted oncall.
samir: grabbing logs. Observable: policy evaluator hit an expression that does indexing into request.user without null checks. Stack snippet:
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 42 [running]:
policy.eval(0xc0003a8000)
	/var/lib/redwood/policy/eval.go:234 +0x1a2
... 
```
samir: Found the offending expression in policy 'smart-region-fallback':
```
# policy DSL snippet
if request.region == "eu" && request.user.preferences["prefer_high_accuracy"] == true {
  route = "eu-high-heap"
}
```
samir: If request.user is nil (requests from internal telemetry), the evaluator tries to index and panics.
jamie: That matches. There was a policy commit this morning that introduced more direct indexing without guards. Repro locally with missing user object.
carla (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) disable the policy 2) flip traffic away from smart routing to stable static routing 3) deploy a hotfix to the evaluator to guard nil accesses. Which is fastest?
jamie: Disable policy via admin API is fastest. Command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://console.redwood/api/v1/policies/smart-region-fallback/disable
# expected response: {"status":"disabled","policy":"smart-region-fallback"}
```
jamie: Also prepare a route override to pin impacted customers to regional pool eu-cluster-high so they avoid fallback loop.
carla (oncall): Executing disable now.
carla (oncall): `curl` returned 200, policy disabled. ops-bot: please broadcast that smart-region-fallback is disabled and routing should be stable.
ops-bot: Broadcast posted to #general and #eng-runtime: "Policy smart-region-fallback disabled for mitigation. Monitoring for error rate normalization." 
maria: Error rate on routes dropped from 7% -> 1.2% in the last 2 minutes. Latency stabilized. Customer reports earliest complaints from customer IDs: cust-41, cust-99, cust-220. Maria: Confirming model_variant mismatch reduced, but some sessions still using gpt-small-quant — those need cleanup.
samir: I pushed a temporary override for the three impacted account IDs to pin model_variant to 'gpt-medium-v2' and region to eu-central via admin route patch:
```
PATCH /api/v1/routing/overrides
[{
  "account_id": "cust-41",
  "region": "eu-central",
  "model_variant": "gpt-medium-v2",
  "expires_in": 3600
}]
```
samir: Responses OK. Affected customers should stop seeing the small variant now.
carla (oncall): Good. I'm going to escalate to eng-runtime for a hotfix ASAP. @leo will you own the hotfix and the compile-time validation? I'll hand off oncall to you in 30m.
leo: Taking it. I'll add nil checks in the evaluator and also add a policy linter that rejects index access into unknown objects (PR coming). Repro test added.
jamie: Suggest adding a safe-access operator in the policy language (like request.user?.preferences) so future rules can't crash the evaluator. But we should also make the evaluator defensive.
leo: Agreed. Short-term: patch to guard map/index with checks. Long-term: language-level opt.
carla (oncall): Customer impact assessment: brief outage-like behavior for some customers: up to 12% request failures for certain endpoints between 1993001098 and 1993001240. ~0.4% of total traffic impacted. No data exfiltration observed. CS notified for the three customers. We'll offer post-incident notes.
maria: CS is prepping outbound messages and tracking complaints. Maria: Slack thread with CS templates: /files/templates/incident/msg-to-customer.md
jamie: Hotfix build created (sha: b3f7a2). Rolling canary to runtime-eu nodes now. Patch includes guard and defensive evaluator wrapper.
ops-bot: Deployment started: rollout id r-8823 to eu cluster. Monitoring health.
leo: Canary looks good, no panics in logs. Rolling to 30% then 100%.
samir: After rollout, searching logs: no further panics. Error rate back to baseline <0.5%.
carla (oncall): Handoff: I need to go offline in 18m. Handover notes: policy disabled, overrides applied, hotfix rolling, customers notified. If the panic resumes, escalate to eng-runtime pager. @leo you're primary now.
leo: Acknowledged. I'll watch through the next 2 hours and create the postmortem doc. Assigning follow-ups: add validator to policy compiler (#PR-4127), add end-to-end test for missing request.user (#TST-9401), update policy authoring guide.
jamie: Quick note: root cause appears to be a policy authoring change merged this morning without linter enforcement. We'll add CI gate to run a policy static analyzer.
carla (oncall): Great work team. Closing mitigation phase; moving to post-incident review. ops-bot, update INC-2026-334 with timeline + notes.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-334 updated: mitigation applied, severity remains P2 until postmortem. Actions: hotfix merged, policy disabled, overrides set, customers notified. Assigned: leo, samir, maria. ETA postmortem draft: 1993002000.
leo: Postmortem start: I'll draft and link to PR/CI items. Also adding a small monitoring alert to detect regressions where policy engine panics > 0 in 5m.
carla (oncall): Thanks all. :thumbsup:
